messages.subject: factor with 4 levels: coding + pre vs post contrasts
messages.subject_clean: factor with 4 levels: coding + pre vs post contrasts
messages.body_plain:
Hello list,

my experiment is a 2X2X4 within subject design, with all three factors being categorical: L=Language of the stimuli (2 levels), V= type of the stimuli (2 levels), D= delay of brain stimulation (4 levels). My dependent variable is the amplitude of a physiological measure.

I will build my maximal mixed model in which all the factors are crossed within subjects and only D is crossed within items (items are the same, repeated at different delays of stimulation):

lmer(MEPzed ~ L * V * D + (L*V*D|subjects) + (D|items), data=mydata, control=lmerControl(optCtrl=list(maxfun=10000)))

and then simplify only the random structure following the guide here: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.04967.pdf

However, before everything, I have to convert the name of the levels of my factors into numbers and set up my contrasts. This is where I'm a bit confused, even after reading the different coding tutorials (I'm a newbie :) ):

for the factor D (delay of stimulation) I would not use Helmert coding because the levels of D are not ordered in our assumptions, while Effect/sum coding could be an option. However, I would stick to the default treatment/dummy coding because, even if we hadn't clear predictions about the delays of stimulation, we thought that the first level could be a reference level.
Nonetheless, I'm also interested in confronting the different delays with each other. In that case I should set up a custom contrast coding, am I right? But I don't know if doing this before or after (post-hoc comparison) the analysis.

So, here are my questions:

q1: is it correct that it's enough to set the contrasts for each factors independently (e.g. L and V--> effect/sum coding, D---> treatment/dummy coding) or should I build an enormous contrast matrix for all the interactions that I'm interested in (e.g. L1V1D1, L1V1D2 etc.) before the ANOVA? In the latter case, can you suggest me how to do it?

q2:- If I use a treatment/dummy contrast for D (i.e. I look into D2-D1 D3-D1 D4-D1), does it make sense that a posteriori I'll look into D2-D3 D2-D4 D3-D4  (corrected by 3 multiple comparison, e.g doing the ANOVA and post-hoc pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model, c("D", "L"), by = "M"))? Or should I directly set all these contrast a priori?

q3:- Secondarily: what's the difference between using D1 as a reference group in treatment coding and really using D1 as a baseline, by subtracting the MEPzed values (i.e. my dependent variable) of D1 from the MEPzed values of D2,3 and 4 in the raw data?


Thank you in advance and please tell me if you need further clarifications or code.

Elisa Monaco | PhD student

messages.body_plain:
Hi Elisa,

this new tutorial paper may answer most or all your questions:

- Schad, D. J., Vasishth, S., Hohenstein, S., & Kliegl, R. (2018). How
  to capitalize on a priori contrasts in linear (mixed) models: A
  tutorial. https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.10451

Best,

  Titus
